NASA_HISTORY.title: A Brief History of the Hubble Space Telescope

claims.claim: Hubble launched in April 1990, above Earth's distorting atmosphere.
claims.result: Verified. Launch and orbital deployment are separate events; the narration gives only the year, 1990.

claims.claim: Incorrect mirror-test setup led to a primary mirror too flat near its outer edge.
claims.result: Verified. No micron measurement or unsupported blame attribution is included.

claims.claim: Spherical aberration made light from different mirror regions focus at different locations.
claims.result: Verified. The focus-knob sentence is an explanatory simplification of a shape error.

claims.claim: The solution compensated optically rather than replacing the primary mirror.
claims.result: Verified. The opening and ending refer specifically to the primary mirror.

claims.claim: COSTAR corrected three existing instruments; WFPC2 had its own internal corrective optics.
claims.result: Verified. COSTAR did not supply WFPC2's correction.

claims.claim: Both systems were installed in December 1993, during a mission with five consecutive spacewalks and other maintenance.
claims.result: Verified. Five spacewalks describes the servicing mission overall, not five walks solely for optics.

claims.claim: Before-and-after M100 images demonstrate improved detail after the repair.
claims.result: Verified in official image captions. Use a WFPC/WFPC2 comparison, not an unrelated modern image.

editorial_notes: Narrative transitions and the closing interpretation are original framing, not quotations or attributed thoughts.
No invented astronaut dialogue, private reactions, client credits, audience figures, or performance claims.
This is a script sample only; it does not supply or license archival footage.
